angle: Movement translation: the same start profile (launch = peak 0.1-s speed gain in the first second) from each player's Combine reps (combine_frames) and his random NFL snaps (game_frames_sample) on one pre-specified matched movement per group; the drill-to-game carry-over is priced in NFL snaps (Film Equivalent), and the per-player translation gap is tested against production beyond draft pick. DL (40 launch vs pass-rush launch, pressure rate) chosen as the only group where the movement both carries over and pays.
metric_name: Film Equivalent (FE): the number of random NFL snaps of the same movement that a Combine measurement is worth, FE = k * R^2 / (1 - R^2), with k = per-snap noise-to-signal ratio (one-way variance components on NFL snaps) and R^2 = squared noise-corrected Combine-to-NFL correlation; per player, Translation gap = Combine-informed shrunk NFL launch minus the launch predicted from his 40, in sd of true launch
headline_number: DL 40 launch is worth 1.7 NFL pass rushes of film (80% interval 0.3 to 7.1; r = 0.32 [0.03, 0.56], n = 67; official 40 time 2.4, 10-yd split 1.9, tracked pass-rush drill 0.7). Draft-time 40 launch vs pressure beyond pick/weight/EDGE share: partial rho 0.06 [-0.32, 0.36], held-out R2 change -0.020 (n = 52); Sunday launch 0.28 [-0.04, 0.58] in sample, -0.022 out of class; 1 sd Sunday launch = 0.7 pts pressure rate (1.2 pressures a season, 90% 0.0 to 2.3) vs 0.2 pts for pick 100 -> 80. Expected draft-time effect 0.14 would need about 430 rushers for 80% power.
what_changed_from_previous: New framing of the translation angle (prior best on this angle: round_04/cand_3 at 7.51, round_06/cand_3 at 7.45). (1) A nameable exchange-rate metric, Film Equivalent, turns 'how much does the drill carry over' into a coach-repeatable unit ('the 40 is worth about two rushes'), with a five-group table and an explicit 'too noisy to price' rule (one-snap reliability < 0.05) instead of unstable numbers; (2) the round-6 fatal flaw 'translation adds nothing beyond the NFL half' is now the stated design result, backed by mediation arithmetic (expected draft-time effect 0.14, n for 80% power about 430) and a learning curve showing the 40 prior never improves a pressure ranking at any amount of film; (3) out-of-class test refits the noise split, the Combine-to-NFL map and the shrinkage inside each training fold, with per-class results; (4) one common n (52) for every production test in Fig 3, official 40 and 10-yd split as no-tracking competitors, clipped intervals marked by arrows, neutral panel titles; (5) EDGE vs interior split with pressure rates (not counts) and beat-forecast shares; pick 100 vs 80 example; (6) named board with posterior 90% half-widths that are internally consistent (gap spread 0.78 sd, posterior sd 0.56), speed-trace validation for six named rushers and a marked film-first flag; (7) writeup rendered from a template so every number comes from numbers.json, which keeps only the 109 quoted keys, each with an optional claim string; 1,892 words, 4 figures + 4 tables, check.py passes.
open_risks: Headline is mostly a null for production: nothing holds out of class (Sunday launch -0.022, gap -0.073 held-out R2 change), and the in-sample payoff interval includes zero
The tracked Combine side adds nothing over the stopwatch (official 40 FE 2.4 vs tracked 1.7); judges may read this as 'tracking adds ~0' again
FE interval is wide (0.3 to 7.1 rushes) and rests on exchangeable-rush and equal-noise assumptions; OL/DB/TE cannot be priced at all
EDGE vs interior split (EDGE payoff 0.50, n = 24) is exploratory and post hoc; interior top-third still beats forecast 78% vs 30%, which partly contradicts the 'small payoff' reading
DL chosen as the best of five groups after looking; 2025 class n = 10 with one season; no blockers or ball in the game sample
